💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone.
  • Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, currently above Juventus and Napoli in the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By FABRIZIO FERRARI FOR DAILY MAIL SPORT.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.

Not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone. It is a town of 42,000 best known for many years as the birthplace of 20th-century screen icon Marcello Mastroianni and global hotelier Carmine Forte, but now the talk of Italian football.

Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, currently above Juventus and Napoli in the table.

Armed with the second-lowest budget in the league, they have regularly started with seven Italian players – the most in the league – including Antonio Raimondo, a 22-year-old striker on loan from Bologna, who scored nine goals in 10 appearances before being halted by injury at the start of this month.

The majority owner is Latest York investment fund Clara Vista, who are part of the consortium behind Ipswich Town, and the head coach is Massimiliano Alvini, who has drawn comparisons to Roberto De Zerbi for both the high-intensity elements of his style and his rise from the humble depths of Italian football.

Only 18 months ago, in May 2025, they looked set to slide into the third tier, bound for a relegation play-off until Brescia were deducted points to hand Frosinone an unlikely stay of execution.

A month later a newly introduced sporting director, Renzo Castagnini, arrived and installed Alvini, who kept faith in most of the squad that had survived only by the skin of its teeth. Survival was again the sole aim. Yet from the very first Coppa Italia fixture Frosinone began to turn heads, beating Monza, a team widely tipped for promotion.

According to recent reports, by the end of the season, they had finished as runners-up behind Venezia and above Monza who were promoted via the play-offs. It was Frosinone’s fourth promotion to Serie A and by far the most beautiful because nobody saw it coming.

Massimiliano Alvini was recognised as the best coach of Serie B at the 35th edition of the FIGC Panchina D'Oro Awards on Monday.

Frosinone Calcio players celebrated their victory against Lecce in October.

Recent findings suggest that much of the credit belongs to Alvini, who was named by his fellow managers on Monday as Serie B’s best coach for 2025-26. The 56-year-old Tuscan played at an amateur level until a serious injury forced him to quit at 30. His coaching career began in the same lowly ranks for Italian football.

Sources indicate that he and his brother Walter sold shoe soles for a living. Increasingly, Walter would be asked to cover at work as his brother followed his newly introduced passion, travelling to study the training sessions of established coaches, including Luciano Spalletti at Roma and Maurizio Sarri at Empoli.

Alvini remains grounded and stubbornly modest despite eight promotions and the sudden spotlight.

If the season ended today, Frosinone would qualify for Europe but perhaps the most incredible part of the story was improvements made last season by individual players who had barely registered in the previous season.

Notably Fares Ghedjemis, who went from scoring two goals to 15. Also Castagnini signings such as Giacomo Calo and others including Giorgi Kvernadze, Gabriele Bracaglia and goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani.

In a recent development, frosinone won 3-0 at Fiorentina, beat Cesc Fabregas’s Como 2-0 and Torino by the same score. At Atalanta – the Europa League winners of 2024 now managed by Sarri – they drew 4-4 and came within a whisker of a late winner.

Twenty points from the first ten games recalled the early bursts of Claudio Ranieri’s newly promoted Fiorentina in 1994-95 and Juventus in 2007-08.

In a recent development, then, in the last fixture before the international break, came a third defeat of the season, at home against Cagliari, despite 29 shots and 13 corners. One of those days when the ball simply refused to go in.

Whether the shareholders of Clara Vista – which bought 80 per cent of Frosinone in the summer – are entirely delighted remains to be seen. There have been suggestions they hoped to see more of the 13 players signed via their data algorithms but only Patrizio Masini and Romano Schmid have been regular starters.

The other nine or 10 names regularly in the starting XI are the same men who drove the climb out of Serie B.

Defensive midfielder Giacomo Calo has scored five goals in 11 games this season.

In a recent development, when it comes to the metric of ‘passes per defensive action’, a key indicator of how rapidly the ball is won back, Frosinone rank among the top four clubs in Europe. The others are Barcelona, Brighton and De Zerbi’s Tottenham.

In a recent development, still, Alvini shrugs off the praise. His first seven years as a coach produced two promotions, one sacking and one relegation. Then a group of friends decided to start a club in the seventh tier (the third amateur level) and put him in charge.

In the seven seasons from 2008 to 2015, Tuttocuoio climbed via four promotions into Serie C.

Alvini moved on to fresh challenges. The next four seasons at Pistoiese and AlbinoLeffe brought his first two professional sackings. He lists them openly on LinkedIn, almost as badges of honour, albeit the second was not a conventional dismissal.

Emergency surgery to insert an artery stent early in the season left him psychologically raw when he returned.

According to recent reports, those three years at AlbinoLeffe however proved formative because he was able to watch Gian Piero Gasperini’s Atalanta methods at close quarters. He took that inspiration into the following campaign at Reggiana, taking them back to Serie B after 21 years for his seventh promotion.

In a recent development, frosinone supplied the eighth and his second taste of Serie A. The first came when he was tempted from Perguia to Cremonese with a team simply not equipped for a relegation scrap. He was sacked by January.

The return is proving sweeter than he could have dared to imagine.

  • En route to setting a points record with 77 points to win the Supporters' Shield, Nashville SC were also led by a record-setting defense that only let the ball into the back of the net 25 times in an entire campaign.

As the MLS Cup playoffs are set to kick off on Thursday, it also means that we are beginning to see who is taking home honors at the end of the season. Nashville SC have already seen Maxwell Woledzi win Defender of the Year, and they have potential honorees up and down the awards docket alongside the youngest MVP finalist in league history, Cavan Sullivan. Antoine Griezmann has also won Newcomer of the Year in only half of a season with Orlando City SC.

Check out the winners and finalists so far:.

With Guilherme receiving MVP votes to become a finalist for the award, it was going to take a special performance for someone else to win Newcomer of the Year, and joining Orlando City SC, Antoine Griezmann did just that. Prior to his arrival, this was a team floundering below the playoff line after moving on from manager Oscar Pareja. In only a half-season, he came in and scored 14 goals and assisted eight more as the first player ever to produce 20 goal contributions in only half a season, while turning this team into contenders. It's going to be tough in the playoffs for Griezmann to overcome the defense, but considering what he has already done with the squad, there's no reason why Orlando should be counted out with the Frenchman next to Justin Ellis.

En route to setting a points record with 77 points to win the Supporters' Shield, Nashville SC were also led by a record-setting defense that only let the ball into the back of the net 25 times in an entire campaign. That success was rewarded with all three finalists for Defender of the Year coming from Nashville, but it's their newest signing that took home the award. Joining from Norwegian club Fredrikstad ahead of the season, Woledzi didn't need much time to adjust, appearing in every regular-season match and helping Nashville build from the back to maintain possession. It was a team effort to tie the MLS clean sheet record with 17 during the season, so it's only natural for one of their defenders to get the honors this season.

With a stylish assist and a gorgeous goal, Viktor Gyokeres produced the sort of match-winning performance that suggests the Swedish striker is making significant progress at last. It has not always been straightforward for him at Arsenal, but this was unquestionably one of his better showings, and it continued an encouraging upturn in his form.

Gyokeres has been the second-choice striker for most of this season, with Mikel Arteta usually preferring the more subtle Kai Havertz in attack. There are signs, though, that Gyokeres is now growing in belief. Following this victory over Slavia Prague, which was much more narrow and nervy than it should have been, he has now scored two goals and registered three assists in his last five appearances.

Even more promising than those statistics was his all-round play in Prague. In the first half especially, Gyokeres held on to long passes, combined with his team-mates and tested the opposition with his runs in behind. For Arsenal’s first goal, he found Noni Madueke with a brilliant pass. For their second, he curled a fabulous strike into the top corner.

Sources indicate that “Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”.

According to recent reports, those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

Sources indicate that “We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” said Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”.

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

According to recent reports, it was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

The goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

One of Slavia’s many problems in a one-sided first half was their inability to cope with Arsenal’s rotations in midfield. That’s the most Arteta has rotated between a Premier League and Champions League game so far this season. Telling perhaps that Konsa, Gabriel and Rice – the team’s defensive bedrock – stay in place. But changes on both sides at full-back, and in the attacking midfield areas.

#59865. Industry News: Why U.S. Soccer's move to name Emma Hayes to the USMNT hiring committee makes sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1991 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Why U.S. Soccer's move to name Emma Hayes to the USMNT hiring committee makes sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.
  • Men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, WASHINGTON, D.C. – By the time U.S. Soccer confirmed Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United early Friday morning, the announcement itself was far from a surprise. The press release included the usual formalities – Steve Cherundolo, the U-23 U.S. men's national team head coach, would fill in for the Dec. 13 friendly against Jamaica that falls outside the FIFA international match calendar, and the assurance that the search for Pochettino's USMNT successor would begin shortly. Federation CEO J.T. Batson and COO Dan Helfrich will unsurprisingly lead the search, as will "the soccer leadership team at U.S. Soccer that includes" assistant sporting director Oguchi Onyewu. There was one unique detail tucked into the announcement, though.

Emma Hayes, the U.S. women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.

Men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event. They operate on different calendars and in the best case scenarios, each team has dedicated members of staff. Hayes' name-drop as news of Pochettino's exit became official, then, is a unicorn-like sighting, even if U.S. Soccer often champions a spirit of collaboration between all of its national teams. It is uncommon for the head coach of one senior national team to help recruit a counterpart but in U.S. Soccer's case, it makes complete sense.

Hayes' coaching career, which spans two decades and two continents, means her inclusion on the federation's soccer leadership team is an obvious one. She is amongst the most respected soccer minds in the game, which easily makes her one of the most important people on U.S. Soccer's payroll no matter how you look at it. That will be especially true in a hiring process that has to conclude with a compelling follow-up act to Pochettino's splashy arrival two years ago. Her perspective might actually be vital in the process, which only adds to the intrigue of what's next for the USMNT.

"We have an extraordinary gift, which is a women's national team manager who's incredibly insightful, bright mind about the sport, who has a set of personal experiences and relationships that span the club and international game, the men's and women's game, the domestic and international club game, and who also has lived in the shoes of what it's like to be a U.S. national team senior coach," Helfrich told CBS Sports on Thursday. "It is a no-brainer that that mind and that voice has a really prominent seat at the table when we're talking about notable moves for the federation.".

Sources indicate that USMNT coaches are rarely style hires; look no further than the list of people to hold the job on a full-time basis this century and the picture paints itself. The only thing Bruce Arena, Bob Bradley, Jurgen Klinsmann, Gregg Berhalter and Pochettino seem to have in common, outside of the job they all once held, is that they were all tasked with some sort of cultural reset depending on the task at hand. That likely will not be the case for Pochettino's successor, though, who will inherit a team with a clear style of play, a healthy mix of veteran players and rising talents and plenty of time on the clock until the next World Cup. The job will be defined in part by continuity, even with the necessary allowance for the new hire to put their unique spin on things.

It has been revealed that that's where Hayes' expertise should play a crucial role, and the same goes for Onyewu. Hayes' tactical know-how makes her as qualified as anyone employed by U.S. Soccer to establish the right stylistic profile for the next USMNT coach, especially with the spirit of continuity in mind. Pochettino's track record with the U.S. team was mixed but at its best, his high-intensity, attack-minded approach suited the player pool really well and continues to do so. Hayes, a tactical pragmatist who prioritized attack-minded teams herself with Chelsea and the USWNT, will be more than able to help match candidates to the player pool they will spend the next several years working with. Hayes admitted as much on Wednesday when addressing the topic for the first time.

Sources indicate that "I work really closely with J.T. in particular and even more so with Dan as we're growing to develop the American soccer movement and J.T. asked if I would be involved as a technical voice, to be involved with the process and I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men's national team coach," she noted. "My role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job, albeit with the women's team, and that I've coached for a number of years and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why and like I said, I feel confident in the group that are being put together. I think it'll be a very thorough process. I think that's the most crucial part of it and like I said, I feel very embedded in what we're doing with the federation so it doesn't feel unusual to me so, like I've said many times, let's build off the good work that Mauricio has done. I think that's the important part and let's get it right.".

That's especially true considering the fact that there are very few slam-dunk candidates to replace Pochettino. Pep Guardiola, months into a sabbatical after a decade with Manchester City, is an obvious target for U.S. Soccer but it is entirely unclear how interested he would be in the vacancy. If he's out of the running, the list of contenders with genuine international appeal dwindles swiftly but it does not necessarily mean the list of worthy candidates vanishes with Guardiola. The hiring committee will need to be strategic in that case, both in terms of creating a list of contenders and then narrowing them down over the interview process, Hayes providing an important perspective along the way.

The jobs of the USMNT and the USWNT head coaches are hardly apples-to-apples but even then, one will still have an acute idea of what the other's job entails. There is inherent value in having a coach help in the process of hiring another coach, since they hold such singular positions – they are often treated as the be-all, end-all when it comes to their team's success, fairly or otherwise. She can also speak to the cadence of national teams, which varies greatly from the club game where coaches essentially work with their players every day during a long season.

"Everyone is aware of the major differences between coaching at the club level and international level, and the main difference is just time on the field and time with your players," Hayes told CBS Sports earlier this year when asked about Pochettino. "Every international coach would love to have more time with their team, but that's not the nature of the international calendar and it's something I know we both had to get used to and are still getting used to … I said a few times that it's almost like we are grandparents. We get to see the players for a week or so and then we send them back to their parents, which is their clubs.".

Outside of her tactical expertise, though, Hayes represents U.S. Soccer's ambitious turn in recent years as much as Pochettino does. She was hired because of her reputation as a serial winner at Chelsea, where she won eight league titles and seven cups. She continued the trend in short order with the USWNT – two months after officially starting in the role, she won Olympic gold at the Paris Games in 2024. U.S. Soccer has equally ambitious goals for the men's team, though the timeline will understandably be longer for that program. They continue to target the USMNT's first World Cup quarterfinal appearance since 2002 but in between, they also hope to medal in the Olympics' men's soccer event, which is contested by U-23 teams, for the first time when the Games come to Los Angeles in 2028. More than many at the federation, Hayes has experience with the intangibles it takes to reach those heights and that's exactly why she was hired in the first place. It also reflects what U.S. Soccer's executives are looking for in the next USMNT head coach.

"The most important characteristic is someone with ambition that matches ours, which is high and so when you have, then, that high shared ambition, then you look for the experience, the talent, the understanding that accompanies that ambition," Helfrich mentioned.

Beyond that, though, Hayes in particular has an idea of what the USMNT job might entail. She is the best of both worlds – she began her coaching career in the U.S. two decades ago and has a deep understanding of the American soccer landscape, but made a name for herself in her native England and can also bring a useful outsider's perspective. There is no perfect equivalent to Hayes waiting for the USMNT job since no coach with experience in the American game has truly broken into the top tiers of the sport just yet, the federation likely to settle for one or the other. Hayes' understanding of both orbits, though, makes her an important guiding force along the way. She might be the only qualified person to answer how much to weigh the insider's perspective with the accomplished outsider's point of view when looking for the next USMNT head coach, in large part because she is the only person who boasts an equal share of it.

In a recent development, hayes' expertise alone means she will be as valuable a sounding board as any, to the point that it's hard to minimize her ability to offer input down to one or two straightforward things. There is one more thing Hayes might have that no one at U.S. Soccer does – easy access to some of the most notable coaches in the game.

Sources indicate that over the course of her successful 12-year tenure at Chelsea, Hayes became one of the most respected coaches in England. She became the first woman to win the Football Writers Association's Tribute Award in 2024 shortly before leaving England for the U.S., and has earned the praise of many of her counterparts in the men's game along the way. Out of anyone at U.S. Soccer, Hayes might actually have the most compelling list of phone numbers in her contacts. She has said Sir Alex Ferguson, a coaching legend if there ever was one after his storied 27-year tenure at Manchester United, calls her "from time to time." Hayes has been in touch with a handful of her contemporaries over the years, including those who have been on U.S. Soccer's radar at one point or another. In her 2024 book, "A Completely Different Game," Hayes said she heard from Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp after having an emergency hysterectomy because of endometriosis in 2022. The pair "sent me long messages, expressing deeply felt emotions," as did Graham Potter and David Moyes.

In a recent development, the rolodex is a covetable one, if ex-U.S. Soccer sporting director Matt Crocker can serve as an example. His greatest accomplishments during his three-year spell, which came to an end in April when he took a similar role with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation, were hiring Hayes and Pochettino. He had previously worked with Pochettino at Southampton a decade earlier, which made U.S. Soccer's approach easier when discussions started. Hayes' value exceeds her ability to hand her bosses a phone number but it is unlikely to go unnoticed at U.S. Soccer, who clearly understands the expertise she would bring to the search in a variety of ways.

What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
  • The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.
  • In a recent development, "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

In a recent development, "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia remarked a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy.".

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," notes Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Recent findings suggest that pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing.".

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

It has been revealed that "I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia mentioned at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

In a recent development, "Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she stated. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases.".

According to recent reports, osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

Industry observers note that she blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist indicates.

Sources indicate that ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on newly introduced US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia.".

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov noted the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

In a recent development, "The concerns discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov remarked.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

Recent findings suggest that "Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," notes Artjom Bronzhukov.

The expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very swiftly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

Sources indicate that "Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but states it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been revealed so far.

Iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

In a recent development, pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the glitch is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

People entering old age now have better memory than their parents did

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.
  • People born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November.
  • In a recent development, the researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.

People born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November. The analysis offers clues about why dementia rates have fallen by 13% per decade over the past 27 years in Europe and the United States2.

In a recent development, the researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words. The study included 219,000 people aged 50 and older who were born between 1910 and 1964, and tracked changes in their scores over three decades. These list-based tests are commonly used to screen for dementia and Alzheimer’s disease.

Consistent with previous studies3, people born more recently entered old age with better memory performance compared with those born in earlier generations. A ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Memory decline also appears to have become less steep across successive generations, says study co-author Anders Fjell, a neuropsychologist at the University of Oslo in Norway.

The findings are “confirmatory” of other studies on the topic, which indicated that the rate of memory decline is slowing down but weren’t statistically significant, says Carol Brayne, an epidemiologist who studies dementia at the University of Cambridge, UK. “It is another piece of the jigsaw.”.

Because many populations around the world are ageing — that is, older individuals are becoming a larger proportion of the total population — the number of people living with dementia is increasing worldwide. But an individual person’s risk of dementia at any given age has dropped by two-thirds over the past 40 years in the United States4. “For those who reach 80, a smaller percentage [of people] will get dementia than before,” explains Fjell.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.

In a recent development, to understand what might be driving this trend, Fjell and his colleagues used longitudinal data on individuals’ cognitive performance to estimate their memory trajectories over time. The authors examined whether people born later in the twentieth century demonstrated differences in their memory performance and their rate of memory decline compared with those born earlier.

The analysis found that with each successive birth decade, people were 64% more likely to maintain stable memory function — that is, experience little or no memory deterioration.

The authors also investigated brain imaging data from nearly 2,000 people over a median of four years. They found that a stable memory during ageing also corresponded to a decrease in shrinkage of the hippocampus — a brain region involved in memory formation.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway.
  • In a recent development, this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m.
  • The commissioner introduced the latest player development rule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's big game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday.

In a recent development, this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also announced a few fresh league rules and future match events.

Here are the latest things coming to NWSL:.

The commissioner introduced the latest player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is at the moment paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways.

"As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," mentioned Berman in her opening remarks.

It has been revealed that "That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an key step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies.".

More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the new player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism.

The addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also confirmed the fresh NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.

"Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This fresh year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she noted.

In a recent development, the NWSL commissioner then announced the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer.

The tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match.

"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a new community," she remarked.

The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.

Fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. Currently, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.

"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite newly introduced audiences," Berman mentioned about heading to Austin.

Sources indicate that commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.

According to recent reports, "Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she said.

Two incoming clubs set for 2028 and new player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights.

And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday.

According to recent reports, "The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us.
  • According to recent reports, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied.
  • The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a new MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

According to recent reports, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

In Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

The parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an issue in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

Sources indicate that in the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

Sources indicate that now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

Okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

Hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

#59851. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (833 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (833 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you.
  • Industry observers note that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday.
  • "We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

Industry observers note that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

In a recent development, his organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

It has been revealed that online games that encourage people to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

It has been revealed that marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these new rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

Industry observers note that for Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

"But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch noted. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests.".

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game.".

In a recent development, for Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he mentioned.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation.".

Recent findings suggest that even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the concerns consumers presently face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she remarked.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding newly introduced rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

BEUC director Agustin Reyna disagrees.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna remarked.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the new legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a organization's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

According to recent reports, the European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

It has been revealed that "It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," mentioned Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

It has been revealed that agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he says. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.

The Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.

Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was declared back in June.

According to recent reports, the Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.

Just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.

Here's everything you need to know about the significant game:.

It has been revealed that date: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160.

The Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals quickly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.

Head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and newly introduced signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit swiftly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.

The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.

"[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman mentioned of the relationship with her teammates.

"I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday.".

Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but rapidly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown. During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.

"I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper said.

Sources indicate that "I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that the Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

#59847. Rivian, Lucid, Scout CEOs aren’t counting on Democrats to restore EV federal support after midterm wins

Rivian, Lucid, Scout CEOs aren’t counting on Democrats to restore EV federal support after midterm wins

💡 Key Takeaways
  • electric vehicle manufacturers stated they're not counting on increased federal support for their businesses once Democrats gain control of Congress in January, but they said they'll gladly take it if it does happen.
  • That was the overall sentiment from CEOs of Rivian Automotive, Lucid Group and EV startup Scout Motors during interviews with CNBC after Democrats' historic midterm election wins.
  • "We've honestly constructed Scout from day one to be in an environment where we're not going to count on, let's say, legislation or count on things that may or may not be there," Scout CEO Scott Keogh, an automotive veteran, told CNBC on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leaders of several U.S. electric vehicle manufacturers stated they're not counting on increased federal support for their businesses once Democrats gain control of Congress in January, but they said they'll gladly take it if it does happen.

That was the overall sentiment from CEOs of Rivian Automotive, Lucid Group and EV startup Scout Motors during interviews with CNBC after Democrats' historic midterm election wins.

"We've honestly constructed Scout from day one to be in an environment where we're not going to count on, let's say, legislation or count on things that may or may not be there," Scout CEO Scott Keogh, an automotive veteran, told CNBC on Wednesday.

According to recent reports, EV makers have had to contend with flip-flopping support from Washington over the years. The Trump administration has ended or rolled back support for climate change initiatives and EVs that were supported by the Biden administration, including an up to $7,500 customer incentive for purchasing an EV.

Legacy automakers such as General Motors and EV startups alike had counted on such credits to help them boost their sales and assist in electric vehicle profitability. But now they don't have that same level of federal assistance.

Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said it's his hope that the Democratic-controlled Congress and Republican President Donald Trump can find middle ground to make progress for the EV industry, but Rivian's not counting on that.

According to recent reports, "We try not to plan for those sort of things. The reality is it's probably going to have less of an impact than we think," Scaringe stated Nov. 6 following the election results. "I think we're going to actually have a lot of challenges getting things done.".

Fellow EV manufacturer Lucid, which is backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, is taking a similar approach.

"You know, they say, 'Blueprint for the worst and … hope for the best.' That's all we can say," Lucid CEO Silvio Napoli told CNBC on Monday. "Anything positive, we'll take it.".

The lack of expected support comes as Democrats seem to be more focused on hot topics such as healthcare and data centers rather than climate change and support for alternative energy technologies such as EVs.

Sources indicate that CNBC previously reported that House Democrats plan to bring to the floor bills reinstating the enhanced health insurance subsidies that expired under the GOP-held Congress and reversing the Medicaid cuts Trump signed into law last year. They also plan to focus on oversight of the Trump administration and affordability.

Rachel McCleery, executive director of the nonprofit policy advisory Coalition for Reimagined Mobility at SAFE, remarked she believes affordability concerns also could include the cost of vehicles, including EVs.

Sources indicate that "I fully expect there will be legislative debates over what to do moving forward, including on EV and EV supply chain incentives," McCleery, a former U.S. Department of Treasury senior advisor and Ford Motor policy director, mentioned. "Bringing down the cost of vehicles for U.S. consumers is top of mind for Democratic policymakers, and electric vehicles are a critical aspect of this agenda because of the multiple challenges greater EV adoption solves for.".

Scout's Keogh said if legislators decide to offer any type of support, he would prefer it to be for EV production, which could then have a trickle-down effect on vehicle pricing and help companies amid inflated costs.

"I always prefer it on the production side," Keogh mentioned. "Anything that can drive down production cost is going to, of course, get passed along to the customer.".

Affordability has been a concern for EV adoption as the vehicles typically cost more than traditional models with internal combustion engines.

Sales of EVs spiked last year ahead of the Trump administration ending the up to $7,500 incentive after September 2025, but have since come down from that high.

According to recent reports, cox Automotive reports the average price for a latest electric vehicle as of September was more than $54,800, according to the most recent available data. That compared to the average overall industry at just over $51,100 last month.

"Ultimately, incentives can help accelerate adoption, but the industry can't build its long-term strategy around them," Stephanie Valdez Streaty, Cox director of industry insight, noted Friday. "The goal has to be making EVs affordable and compelling enough that they make sense for more consumers with or without an incentive.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized blueprint is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized blueprint is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Industry observers note that rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

It has been revealed that rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

In a recent development, "I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she noted Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

Industry observers note that five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

Sources indicate that "I'm so excited," she said. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

Recent findings suggest that "She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

"I am excited to go in every day," Morgan said. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

"We have these significant red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan stated. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

"I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman stated. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many fresh players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

According to recent reports, "Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone said. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a newly introduced construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

In a recent development, "Obviously, it was incredibly key for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

Recent findings suggest that "She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] Newly introduced York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

In a recent development, "She's fun, she's engaging," Stone remarked. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

According to recent reports, rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

"Trin is a generational talent," Stone noted. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".
